1. Mao, Shi, Zhu, 'Proof of Almkvist's conjecture on the unimodality of partition polynomials', arXiv:2609.23779 (2026-09-20), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23779 . Abstract: 'For integers $r\ge2$ and $n\ge1$, let $F_{r,n}(q)=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1-q^{rk}}{1-q^k}$. ... Almkvist conjectured that $F_{r,n}(q)$ is unimodal in the following two cases: every even $r$ and every $n\ge 1$; every odd $r$ and every $n\ge 11$. He proved that this conjecture is true for $3\le r \le 20$ and $r=100,101$. In this paper, we completely settle the conjecture.' Theorem 1.3 (HTML): 'Let r >= 2 and n >= 1 be integers. Then F_{r,n}(q) is unimodal whenever r is even or n >= 11.' Method (HTML, intro): 'In Section 2, we establish preliminary results on the symmetry and first differences of the coefficients, and derive an induction criterion for unimodality. ... Section 4 proves Conjecture 1.1 for n >= 12. We use Fourier inversion to estimate the first differences of the coefficient sequence in the required range directly. Local estimates near roots of unity, together with a contraction bound ...'. Relation: 文献连线 for R5/R6 (first-difference + roots-of-unity analysis of products of stretched q-integers; stabilization in n); the family has no ordinary factors and is not P(q). Supersedes the Almkvist 1989 partial result cited in round 3.

2. CIMSY arXiv:2605.12822, verification statement not quoted in round 3 (cimsy/main.tex l.1273): 'We have computationally verified \Cref{conj:unimodalitylemma} for $k \leq 5, \pow \leq 6$ and $\max\{a_i,b\} \leq 15$. In general, the condition is not necessary: $([3]_q)^4 [2]_{q^4}$ is unimodal despite violating the inequality ...' (\pow = r). Also the conjecture text itself (l.1265-1271): 'Let $\pow \geq2, k \geq 1$ and let $a_1,\ldots, a_k,b$ be positive integers. Then if $\pow \mid a_i$ for any $1 \leq i \leq k$ or $b \leq 1+\sum_{i=1}^{k}\left\lfloor\frac{a_i}{\pow}\right\rfloor$, the polynomial $[a_1]_q\dots[a_k]_q[b]_{q^{\pow}}$ is unimodal. Moreover, if $k \leq 3$ or $\pow \leq 3$, this condition is also necessary.' and the k=2, r=2 theorem (l.1161): 'For any $a, b,c \in \mathbb{N}$, $T(q)=[a]_q[b]_q[c]_{q^2}$ is symmetric and unimodal if and only if $2c \leq a+b$ or $a$ or $b$ is even.' Relevant to the new S2 claims for r=4,5,6 (published sufficiency-check box) and to R2/R3.

3. Adjacent partition-polynomial family results (background for R5/R6, same Odlyzko-Richmond analytic method, no ordinary factors): Guo-Zhu, 'Unimodality of Certain Partition Polynomials', J. Syst. Sci.
